title: Trendlines and Channels
lessons/trend-u2-l1/steps/0/body: An **uptrend line** connects at least **two higher lows** and sits below price. As long as price stays above it, the uptrend is healthy and the line acts as **dynamic support**.
lessons/trend-u2-l1/steps/1/title: The downtrend line and the third touch
lessons/trend-u2-l1/steps/1/body: A **downtrend line** connects **lower highs** and sits above price like **dynamic resistance**. You can draw a line through any two points; a **third touch** shows the market really respects it.
lessons/trend-u2-l1/steps/2/prompt: What role does this line play for price?
lessons/trend-u2-l1/steps/2/explanation: The line runs through two higher lows and slopes up beneath price. It's an uptrend line, and every time price came back to it, it acted as support.
lessons/trend-u2-l1/steps/3/prompt: The trendline is drawn from the first two lows. Tap the candle that touched it a third time and bounced.
lessons/trend-u2-l1/steps/3/explanation: This candle's lower wick touched the trendline exactly and it closed green. A third touch makes the line more reliable, and price kept climbing after it.
lessons/trend-u2-l1/steps/4/statement: To draw an uptrend line, you connect the price highs.
lessons/trend-u2-l1/steps/4/explanation: An uptrend line connects higher lows and sits below price. Connecting highs is for a downtrend line (or the top of a channel).
lessons/trend-u2-l1/steps/5/body: The **more touches** a trendline has, the more reliable it is. **Very steep** lines tend to break quickly. Draw on wicks or on bodies, but **be consistent**, and never force a line onto the chart.
lessons/trend-u2-l1/steps/5/tip: If your line has to cut through a bunch of candles, that line doesn't exist.
lessons/trend-u2-l1/steps/6/options/0: One touched 4 times, with price bouncing each time
lessons/trend-u2-l1/steps/6/options/1: One that passes through a single low
lessons/trend-u2-l1/steps/6/options/2: One that cuts through the bodies of several candles
lessons/trend-u2-l1/steps/6/explanation: Each touch means buyers (or sellers) defended the line once more. One point can't make a line, and very steep lines rarely last.
lessons/trend-u2-l1/steps/7/prompt: In an uptrend, Ethereum came back to the trendline and closed green on it. What do you do?
lessons/trend-u2-l1/steps/7/explanation: The trend is up and price bounced off the trendline for the third time. A continuation is more likely, so buying near the line with a tight stop (below it) makes sense. Of course, the line could break at any moment.
lessons/trend-u2-l1/steps/8/sentence: A downtrend line connects lower ___ and acts as dynamic ___.
lessons/trend-u2-l1/steps/8/explanation: In a downtrend the highs keep getting lower. A line through them sits above price and keeps it from rising.
lessons/trend-u2-l2/steps/0/body: A **channel** is two roughly **parallel** lines with price swinging between them. In a **rising channel**, the lower line is the trendline (through the lows), and the upper line runs parallel to it through the highs.
lessons/trend-u2-l2/steps/1/body: In a **falling channel**, both lines point down: highs and lows keep getting lower. A **horizontal channel** is just a **range**: price goes back and forth between a fairly flat support and resistance.
lessons/trend-u2-l2/steps/2/prompt: What kind of channel is this?
lessons/trend-u2-l2/steps/2/explanation: Two parallel lines, both pointing down: highs and lows keep getting lower. That's a falling channel.
lessons/trend-u2-l2/steps/3/prompt: The channel's lower line is drawn from the first two lows. Tap the candle that bounced off the channel floor a third time.
lessons/trend-u2-l2/steps/3/explanation: This candle's wick reached the lower channel line and it closed green. In a rising channel, the floor is where buyers usually step back in.
lessons/trend-u2-l2/steps/4/statement: In a rising channel, the upper and lower lines are roughly parallel.
lessons/trend-u2-l2/steps/4/explanation: That's what makes it a channel. If the two lines converge, it's no longer a channel; you're looking at patterns like a triangle or a wedge.
lessons/trend-u2-l2/steps/5/body: In a rising channel, many traders **buy near the channel floor** and target the **channel top**, with a stop loss just below the channel. If price **stops reaching the top**, buyers are getting weak.
lessons/trend-u2-l2/steps/6/prompt: USD/JPY is in a falling channel and price has reached the channel top. The last candle has a long upper wick. What do you do?
lessons/trend-u2-l2/steps/6/explanation: The channel is falling and price got rejected at the top, so a move back toward the floor is more likely. Selling near the top, with the trend and a stop just above the channel, makes sense.
lessons/trend-u2-l2/steps/7/prompt: In Bitcoin's rising channel, you bought near the floor. What's your risk-to-reward up to the channel top?
lessons/trend-u2-l2/steps/7/explanation: Risk = 60,300 − 59,700 = 600 and reward = 62,100 − 60,300 = 1,800. For every 1 unit of risk, you're aiming for 3 units of profit: 1:3.
lessons/trend-u2-l2/steps/8/pairs/2/mean: A range between support and resistance
lessons/trend-u2-l2/steps/8/pairs/3/mean: A line connecting lows or highs
lessons/trend-u2-l3/steps/0/body: When a candle **closes with its body below an uptrend line**, we say the line has broken. If only the **wick** pokes through and the candle closes above the line, no break is confirmed yet.
lessons/trend-u2-l3/steps/1/body: After a break, price often **comes back to test the line from below**. Now the line that was support acts as **resistance**. Many traders wait for this **pullback** to enter with less risk.
lessons/trend-u2-l3/steps/2/prompt: Tap the candle that truly broke the trendline (with a close).
lessons/trend-u2-l3/steps/2/explanation: The candle in the middle of the chart only dipped below the line with its wick and closed above it; that wasn't a break. This candle closed with its body below the line. That's the real break.
lessons/trend-u2-l3/steps/3/statement: Every time a candle's wick pokes through the trendline, the trend is over.
lessons/trend-u2-l3/steps/3/explanation: A wick means price crossed briefly but came back. A valid break is when the candle's body closes on the other side of the line, and even then a reversal isn't certain.
lessons/trend-u2-l3/steps/4/prompt: After the trendline broke, price climbed back up to just below the line. What is this move?
lessons/trend-u2-l3/steps/4/options/0/la: A pullback to the broken line
lessons/trend-u2-l3/steps/4/options/2/la: A third touch of the trendline
lessons/trend-u2-l3/steps/4/explanation: The trendline broke on a close a few candles ago, and now price has come back up to test it from below. That's a pullback, and the broken line can now act as resistance.
lessons/trend-u2-l3/steps/5/title: A break means weakness, not a sure reversal
lessons/trend-u2-l3/steps/5/body: A trendline break means **the trend has weakened**, not necessarily that it has flipped. After a break, price may **range** or even continue the old trend. For more confirmation, look at **structure** (new highs and lows) and the pullback.
lessons/trend-u2-l3/steps/5/tip: After an uptrend line breaks, be extra careful with new buys. Conditions have changed.
lessons/trend-u2-l3/steps/6/prompt: GBP/USD broke its uptrend line, came back up under it and printed a shooting star. What do you do?
lessons/trend-u2-l3/steps/6/explanation: The line broke, price pulled back to it and printed a shooting star below it, so the line is now acting as resistance. A further drop is more likely. Stop loss above the shooting star's high.
lessons/trend-u2-l3/steps/7/prompt: Put the steps of trading an uptrend line break in order.
lessons/trend-u2-l3/steps/7/items/0: An uptrend with a reliable trendline
lessons/trend-u2-l3/steps/7/items/1: A candle closes below the trendline
lessons/trend-u2-l3/steps/7/items/2: Price pulls back to the broken line
lessons/trend-u2-l3/steps/7/items/3: Price gets rejected at the line and you sell
lessons/trend-u2-l3/steps/7/explanation: First you need a reliable line, then a break on a close, then a pullback, and finally a sign of rejection at the line for your entry.
lessons/trend-u2-l3/steps/8/prompt: Why do many traders wait for a pullback after a trendline break?
lessons/trend-u2-l3/steps/8/options/0: Better entry, smaller stop, and it filters out some fake breaks
lessons/trend-u2-l3/steps/8/options/1: Because a pullback always follows every break
lessons/trend-u2-l3/steps/8/options/2: Because there's no risk left after a pullback
lessons/trend-u2-l3/steps/8/options/3: Because a trendline break means nothing on its own
lessons/trend-u2-l3/steps/8/explanation: A pullback gives a better entry price and a tighter stop. But it doesn't always happen; sometimes price takes off without one, and you have to accept that.
lessons/trend-u2-l3/steps/9/sentence: After an uptrend line breaks, the broken line usually acts as ___, and price coming back to it is called a ___.
lessons/trend-u2-l3/steps/9/explanation: Broken support often turns into resistance, and retesting it from below is called a pullback.
